newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT - TCI splits up cable systems.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT - TCI splits up cable systems.

text.p: TCI Communications Inc said on Wednesday that it will split its cable operations into three groups to focus on the individual needs of each group.
It said more announcements on related organizational changes will follow shortly.
The following is a full text of its press release.

ENGLEWOOD, Colo., Oct. 30 /PRNewswire/ -- TCI Communications, Inc. today announced that its cable operations will be organized into three separate operating groups. The company has created this new structure to pursue its continuing strategy of creating new technology solutions for categories of systems with similar needs.

Group A will consist of a large group of cable systems in various urban and metro markets that are preparing to offer new services on advanced cable systems. Barry Marshall, now Executive Vice President of TCI's cable operations, will be the President of Group A.

Group B will consist of cable systems where TCI's digital TV product, ALL TV, can be opportunistically deployed. In many of these systems, TCI's terrestrial digital TV product will be the appropriate solution to bring new technologies to TCI customers in these areas. The President of Group B will be Marvin Jones, formerly with Liberty Media and United Artists cable, and a 38-year veteran of the cable industry.

Group C will consist of those systems in Hartford, the Chicago suburbs and parts of the San Francisco Bay area in which the company has previously announced its intention to offer integrated delivery of its core cable product, ALL TV (digital TV product), People Link by TCI (wireline telephone service) and Home (Internet services). Barbara Mowry, now Senior Vice President of Customer Satisfaction, will be the President of Group C.

"This organization allows us to strongly focus on the differing individual needs of each system group, and to take further advantage of advances in our terrestrial digital television program," said Brendan Clouston, President and CEO of TCI Communications, Inc. "This new organization will help us deploy ALL TV faster. It also will help us devise winning competitive strategies for categories of systems that have common business, regulatory and operating environments."

The management and organizational changes that will help drive this new structure will be announced shortly. Likewise, the company will announce very soon where individual cable systems fit within this structure.

Tele-Communications, Inc. is traded through TCI Group and the Liberty Media Group Common Stocks. TCI Group is traded on The Nasdaq National Market through its Series A and Series B TCI Group Common Stock, under the symbols TCOMA and TCOMB, respectively. Liberty Media Group is traded with Series A and Series B Common Stock, under the symbols LBTYA and LBTYB, respectively. TCI Group is a majority stockholder in Tele-Communications International, Inc., which is traded under the symbol TINTA. TCI Communications, Inc., the Company's domestic communications subsidiary, trades its Cumulative Exchangeable Preferred Stock, Series A on The Nasdaq National Market under the symbol TCICP and its Trust Originated Preferred Securities ("TOPrS") trades on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol TFI/pr.
